01 / Introduction

Introduction and mathematical scope

An implied volatility surface expresses a collection of European option prices in a common coordinate system. Its construction is an inverse problem, a statistical estimation problem and a problem of economic consistency.

In Black–Scholes Option Pricing, volatility was an input and the option premium an output. Here the direction is reversed: a premium, a strike, an expiry and a financing convention determine an implied volatility. Repeating that inversion across contracts produces a smile for each expiry and a surface across expiries. A surface can be useful even when the constant-volatility assumptions behind the quoting formula are unrealistic.

Three objects must remain distinct. A quoted implied volatility is a contract-level price coordinate. A fitted surface estimates missing prices between observations. A dynamic model specifies how prices and uncertainty evolve through time. Agreement with today's vanilla prices does not uniquely determine future smile behavior or the value of every path-dependent payoff.

An analogy: converting a map to a common scale

Different option premiums resemble measurements taken with different rulers. A short-dated out-of-the-money call and a long-dated at-the-money call cannot be compared by premium alone. Implied volatility translates each measurement using its contract specifications. A common map becomes easier to read, but a translation does not remove measurement error or explain how the landscape changes tomorrow.

Organization of the notes

Part I develops the price inversion, coordinates, term structure and market-data conventions. Part II establishes static-arbitrage restrictions, interpolation, SVI/SSVI parameterizations, calibration and extrapolation. Part III connects the surface to local volatility, stochastic models and risk management, then develops an interactive laboratory, numerical studies, an appendix and exercises.

The core framework uses strictly positive forwards, deterministic discounting, European exercise and proportional carry. It permits negative interest rates provided discount factors remain positive. Discrete dividends, early exercise, negative forwards and event jumps require additional treatment; later chapters explain where the central framework stops applying.

Numerical conventions

Volatility is stored as an annualized decimal: 24% is 0.24. Time is measured in year fractions. A volatility percentage point is 0.01; a volatility basis point is 0.0001. Premiums are per unit of underlying, without a contract multiplier. All numerical option chains and surface experiments on this page are synthetic. They illustrate reproducible methods and do not represent live exchange quotes.

The reference surface uses a short variance-rate scale of 24%, a long scale of 18%, a decay time of 1.2 years, asymmetry parameter −0.65 and shape scale 2.3. Its formulas and derivative checks are explicit. Static figures retain their numerical data, and the laboratory allows the parameters to be changed without a network connection.

Elementary calculus, normal probabilities and European option pricing are the main prerequisites. A reader can follow the data and calibration discussion before studying the density and local-volatility derivations. The mathematical appendix supplies the derivatives needed to reproduce the diagnostics.

02 / Pricing conventions

Forward-based European option valuation

Let S0S_0 denote spot, T>0T>0 maturity, D(T)>0D(T)>0 the discount factor and F(T)>0F(T)>0 the forward price. With constant continuously compounded rate rr and proportional dividend yield qq, D(T)=e−rTD(T)=e^{-rT} and F(T)=S0e(r−q)TF(T)=S_0e^{(r-q)T}. Separating the forward from discounting makes the same pricing formula applicable to many European spot and futures options, subject to their actual settlement conventions.

CB=D(T)[F(T)Φ(d1)−KΦ(d2)],d1=ln(F(T)/K)+12σ2TσT,d2=d1−σT.C_{\mathrm{B}}=D(T)\left[F(T)\Phi(d_1)-K\Phi(d_2)\right],\qquad d_1=\frac{\ln(F(T)/K)+\frac{1}{2}\sigma^2T}{\sigma\sqrt T},\quad d_2=d_1-\sigma\sqrt T.
(01)

Here K>0K>0 is strike and Φ\Phi the standard normal distribution function. The corresponding put follows either from the direct formula or European put–call parity:

PB=D(T)[KΦ(−d2)−F(T)Φ(−d1)],CB−PB=D(T)(F(T)−K).P_{\mathrm{B}}=D(T)\left[K\Phi(-d_2)-F(T)\Phi(-d_1)\right],\qquad C_{\mathrm{B}}-P_{\mathrm{B}}=D(T)(F(T)-K).
(02)

The forward as the center of the smile

Forward at-the-money means K=F(T)K=F(T). It need not mean K=S0K=S_0, and neither definition necessarily coincides with a 50-delta contract. Rate and dividend differences make the center expiry dependent. Using spot moneyness for one expiry and forward moneyness for another introduces a coordinate shift that can resemble a change in skew.

A premium can be normalized by D(T)F(T)D(T)F(T). Let k=ln(K/F(T))k=\ln(K/F(T)) and w=σ2Tw=\sigma^2T. The normalized call is a function of just these two variables:

c(k,w)=CBD(T)F(T)=Φ(−kw+w2)−ekΦ(−kw−w2).c(k,w)=\frac{C_{\mathrm{B}}}{D(T)F(T)} =\Phi\left(-\frac{k}{\sqrt w}+\frac{\sqrt w}{2}\right) -e^k\Phi\left(-\frac{k}{\sqrt w}-\frac{\sqrt w}{2}\right).
(03)

This reduction is helpful for inversion and surface analysis. Forward and discount inputs determine the translation into normalized prices; the smile describes the remaining strike-dependent variation. It does not make inaccurate carry inputs harmless.

Boundary cases and units

At zero variance, the call is Dmax(F−K,0)D\max(F-K,0). At increasing variance, the call approaches DFDF; the put approaches DKDK. At expiry, the volatility coordinate ceases to identify a time distribution, and the payoff is determined by the terminal price. Handle these limits separately rather than dividing by zero in d1d_1.

Black vega, holding the forward and discount factor fixed, is DFφ(d1)TDF\varphi(d_1)\sqrt T, where φ\varphi is the normal density. It measures premium change per unit decimal volatility. A quoted vega of 38 per unit means approximately 0.38 premium units for a one-percentage-point volatility move. Contract multipliers scale both the premium and vega.

For American exercise, the same inversion is generally inappropriate because the quoted premium may include early-exercise value. For a normal or shifted-lognormal quoting convention, the numerical implied-volatility value has a different meaning. A database field called “IV” is incomplete without its valuation model and conventions.

03 / Inverse valuation

Implied volatility: existence and uniqueness

For fixed positive F,K,D,TF,K,D,T, the implied volatility is the nonnegative parameter that reproduces the observed European premium in the Black formula. It is not an additional observation of future realized volatility; it is defined through the observed price and chosen inputs.

CB(F,K,D,T,σimp)=Cobs,∂CB∂σ=DFφ(d1)T>0for σ>0.C_{\mathrm{B}}(F,K,D,T,\sigma_{\mathrm{imp}})=C_{\mathrm{obs}},\qquad \frac{\partial C_{\mathrm{B}}}{\partial\sigma}=DF\varphi(d_1)\sqrt T>0 \quad\text{for }\sigma>0.
(04)

Strict positive vega makes the mapping strictly increasing. Its lower and upper limits establish the finite-volatility domain:

Dmax(F−K,0)≤Cobs<DF,Dmax(K−F,0)≤Pobs<DK.D\max(F-K,0)\le C_{\mathrm{obs}}<DF,\qquad D\max(K-F,0)\le P_{\mathrm{obs}}<DK.
(05)

Interpreting the boundaries

A price equal to the lower bound has the limiting implied volatility zero. An interior price has a unique strictly positive finite value. The upper bound is approached only as volatility tends to infinity, so an exact price at that bound has no finite implied volatility. A quote outside the interval cannot be repaired by a better root solver: either its inputs, conventions or price are inconsistent.

Near the intrinsic boundary, premium precision can be insufficient to resolve a small time value. A displayed quote may equal the lower bound because of rounding, even if its economic volatility is positive. A zero numerical IV in this situation describes the resolution of the input, not evidence that the underlying will be deterministic.

Calls and puts should agree under matched inputs

Under European parity, calls and puts with the same strike and expiry recover the same implied volatility. When they do not, investigate asynchronous quotes, different dividend assumptions, settlement differences, stale prices and exercise style. A separate call surface and put surface can conceal a common forward error.

The out-of-the-money side often offers more useful numerical information because an in-the-money premium contains a large intrinsic component. For K<FK<F, a put is out of the money; for K>FK>F, a call is out of the money. Converting through parity removes the intrinsic component, but the carry inputs and quote uncertainty still matter.

Implied volatility and expectations

The option price is a discounted risk-neutral expectation of a nonlinear payoff. Implied volatility condenses that expectation into one Black parameter. Different distributions can generate the same premium for one contract. The volatility risk premium, nonlinear payoff weighting and smile shape prevent a general equality between this coordinate and the physical expected standard deviation of future returns.

A full continuum of option prices reveals substantially more information than one implied volatility, but even a complete terminal distribution does not determine the joint distribution of prices at several future dates. This distinction will matter when moving from vanilla calibration to exotic pricing.

04 / Numerical analysis

Numerical inversion and conditioning

Define the residual f(σ)=CB(σ)−Cobsf(\sigma)=C_{\mathrm{B}}(\sigma)-C_{\mathrm{obs}}. A dependable solver begins by checking the premium bounds, then finds a bracket with opposite residual signs. Because the price map is monotone, bisection gives a simple reliable reference implementation. Brent's method combines bracketing with interpolation and is useful in production implementations.

Bracketed and Newton iterations

Choose a positive upper volatility, increase it until the model price is above the observation, and retain zero or a small positive value as the lower endpoint. At each bisection step evaluate the midpoint and replace the endpoint with the same residual sign. The bracket width halves at each iteration, providing a direct volatility-error bound.

σn+1=σn−CB(σn)−CobsDFφ(d1(σn))T.\sigma_{n+1}=\sigma_n- \frac{C_{\mathrm{B}}(\sigma_n)-C_{\mathrm{obs}}} {DF\varphi(d_1(\sigma_n))\sqrt T}.
(06)

Newton's update is fast near a well-conditioned root. It may take a negative or excessively large step when vega is small. A safeguarded implementation keeps the bracket and replaces unsafe Newton steps with bisection. Use a finite iteration limit and return an explicit failure state if the bracket cannot be established within the chosen volatility cap.

A very small price residual does not always imply an accurate volatility. Conversely, insisting on microscopic volatility error may be pointless when the quoted premium has a wide bid–ask interval. Report a solver tolerance separately from input uncertainty.

Local sensitivity of the inverse map

Differentiating the defining equation at fixed inputs gives:

∂σimp∂C=1Vega,Δσimp≈ΔCVega.\frac{\partial\sigma_{\mathrm{imp}}}{\partial C} =\frac{1}{\operatorname{Vega}},\qquad \Delta\sigma_{\mathrm{imp}}\approx\frac{\Delta C}{\operatorname{Vega}}.
(07)

This explains why short-dated wings can display large IV changes from a single premium tick. The effect is mathematical conditioning, not necessarily a dramatic revision to the market's uncertainty assessment. A premium half-spread of 0.02 with vega 2 implies approximately one volatility percentage point of uncertainty; with vega 40 it implies 0.05 percentage points.

Precision and validation

Deep in-the-money call formulas subtract substantial terms. Prefer parity-based out-of-the-money evaluation and numerically stable normal-tail functions. In extreme tails, underflow can turn a small positive option value into zero. Such cases should be marked unresolved at the working precision rather than assigned a supposedly exact root.

Test inversion by generating premiums from known volatilities across strikes and expiries, then recovering those values. Also test invalid premiums, exact intrinsic limits, near-upper-bound prices, negative rates, and call–put parity. Round-trip errors measure implementation consistency; comparison with an independent pricing and root-solving library gives stronger evidence than using the same function twice.

The laboratory uses a bracketed solver on synthetic prices and reports a root for its selected contract. Its static numerical studies use SciPy's normal distribution and Brent solver as an independent reference. The displayed surface itself is specified analytically, so inversion is an explicit demonstration of the price-to-coordinate conversion.

05 / Surface coordinates

Moneyness, delta and total-variance coordinates

A surface may be expressed as σ(K,T)\sigma(K,T), σ(K/F(T),T)\sigma(K/F(T),T), σ(k,T)\sigma(k,T) or a delta-based quotation. Each representation describes contracts differently. Make the coordinate choice explicit before comparing expiries or building interpolation rules.

k=ln(KF(T)),w(k,T)=Tσimp(k,T)2,σimp(k,T)=w(k,T)T.k=\ln\left(\frac{K}{F(T)}\right),\qquad w(k,T)=T\,\sigma_{\mathrm{imp}}(k,T)^2,\qquad \sigma_{\mathrm{imp}}(k,T)=\sqrt{\frac{w(k,T)}{T}}.
(08)

Total variance is dimensionless under the annualized-volatility convention. It measures the variance budget encoded by the Black quote, without asserting that every smile point is the expected realized quadratic variation of one process. It is especially useful because calendar restrictions concern accumulated variance rather than annualized volatility alone.

Spot and forward moneyness

The logarithmic coordinates satisfy ln(K/S0)=k+ln(F(T)/S0)\ln(K/S_0)=k+\ln(F(T)/S_0). Carry therefore shifts a spot-moneyness plot horizontally by an expiry-dependent amount. A fixed kk across expiries corresponds to a fixed strike-to-forward ratio, not necessarily a fixed absolute strike. This difference is central to the correct formulation of calendar-arbitrage checks with nonzero carry.

Log-moneyness converts multiplicative strike changes into additive coordinates and treats reciprocal ratios symmetrically. A strike 20% above the forward has k=ln(1.2)k=\ln(1.2), approximately 0.1823. A strike 20% below has ln(0.8)\ln(0.8), approximately −0.2231; equal percentage deviations are not equal log deviations.

Delta quotations

Black forward call delta is Φ(d1)\Phi(d_1); spot call delta under proportional yield is e−qTΦ(d1)e^{-qT}\Phi(d_1). Futures, foreign-exchange and premium-adjusted conventions may use other definitions. A “25-delta put” cannot be translated into a strike without knowing the delta convention, forward, expiry and implied volatility used in the conversion.

A delta coordinate depends on the volatility being solved for, making conversion implicit. At K=FK=F, d1=σT/2>0d_1=\sigma\sqrt T/2>0, so the forward call delta exceeds 0.5. Under constant volatility, the forward 50-delta strike is Few/2F e^{w/2}. With a smile, that relation uses the volatility at the unknown strike and requires a numerical solution.

Choice of display and choice of model

A plot in volatility units is intuitive, while fitting in total variance often makes consistency easier to control. A risk report may use delta buckets because those align with quoting practice. None of these displays grants arbitrage freedom. Validate the resulting option prices and the appropriate total-variance restrictions after conversion.

The numerical plots use forward log-moneyness unless their axes explicitly say strike. The interactive heatmap reports the actual maturity and log-moneyness of each sampled cell. Its maturity slices retain all curves at a shared horizontal coordinate, so a reader can inspect cross-expiry values without comparing different strikes accidentally.

06 / Smile geometry

Volatility smiles, skews and economic interpretation

A smile is the implied-volatility curve across strikes at one expiry. A symmetric smile has higher volatility in both wings than near its center. A skew is an asymmetric pattern; a downward equity-style skew often assigns higher implied volatility to lower strikes. These names describe geometry and do not establish a universal mechanism.

Level, slope and curvature

The level measures the magnitude of implied volatility near a reference strike. The local skew is a first derivative, such as ∂kσ(0,T)\partial_k\sigma(0,T). Smile curvature is a second derivative. These are coordinate dependent: derivatives with respect to strike, log-moneyness and delta have different scales.

∂σ∂k=wk2Tw,∂2σ∂k2=wkk2Tw−wk24Tw3/2.\frac{\partial\sigma}{\partial k}=\frac{w_k}{2\sqrt{Tw}},\qquad \frac{\partial^2\sigma}{\partial k^2} =\frac{w_{kk}}{2\sqrt{Tw}}-\frac{w_k^2}{4\sqrt T\,w^{3/2}}.
(09)

A positive curvature in total variance need not imply the same sign in volatility because the square root contributes a negative term. Likewise, a smooth convex-looking volatility plot does not directly establish convexity of call prices. The latter is the economically relevant butterfly condition.

Possible economic drivers

Asymmetric return distributions, price–volatility dependence, jumps, demand for protection, funding constraints and the pricing of volatility risk can all affect a smile. A downturn may increase leverage ratios or coincide with more uncertainty, motivating models with negative price–variance correlation. The same observed skew can nevertheless be generated by several different dynamic models.

Demand for downside protection can influence prices relative to a frictionless model. It does not mean that low-strike implied volatility equals a literal physical probability of a crash. The premium combines payoff magnitude, discounting, risk-neutral weighting and the distribution of terminal prices. Extracting physical probabilities requires further assumptions or data.

Risk reversals and butterflies as quote summaries

A risk reversal is often the difference between call and put IV at matched delta magnitudes. A quoted volatility butterfly is often the average of wing IVs minus ATM IV. Exact definitions vary by market and may involve premium-neutral packages or broker-specific conventions. These quotations are not identical to the payoff-based strike butterfly used to test price convexity.

Write the quotation formula and delta convention before reconstructing a smile from ATM, risk-reversal and butterfly inputs. Inferring wing strikes with one convention and valuing them with another creates a systematic calibration error. Quote summaries are convenient sparse observations, not a complete arbitrage constraint system.

Comparing smiles through time

Fixing absolute strike, log-moneyness or delta leads to different time series when the underlying moves. A decline in spot can move a fixed strike from one part of the smile to another even if the surface in log-moneyness coordinates is unchanged. State the reference coordinate when describing a “volatility increase.”

The laboratory's asymmetry parameter changes a synthetic family of smiles. It is a shape parameter of the selected representation. Interpreting it as the directly observed correlation of price and physical volatility would require a dynamic model and an estimation procedure that are absent from this static example.

07 / Expiry dependence

Maturity structure and forward variance

Annualized implied volatility can increase or decrease with maturity. Short-dated options may concentrate exposure to an imminent event, while long-dated prices average uncertainty over a larger interval. Calendar consistency therefore cannot be tested by requiring volatility itself to increase.

In a deterministic time-dependent volatility model with no smile, the Black total variance equals integrated instantaneous variance. This special case gives a useful interpretation of maturity interpolation:

w(T)=∫0Tv(t)dt,σimp(T)2=1T∫0Tv(t)dt,v(T)=dw(T)dT.w(T)=\int_0^T v(t)\,dt,\qquad \sigma_{\mathrm{imp}}(T)^2=\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T v(t)\,dt,\qquad v(T)=\frac{dw(T)}{dT}.
(10)

For two maturities, the implied forward variance budget in that model is:

vT1,T2=w(T2)−w(T1)T2−T1,T2>T1.v_{T_1,T_2}=\frac{w(T_2)-w(T_1)}{T_2-T_1},\qquad T_2>T_1.
(11)

If six-month volatility is 30% and one-year volatility is 25%, total variances are 0.045 and 0.0625. The later half-year variance rate is 0.035, with square root approximately 18.71%. Falling annualized volatility is entirely compatible with positive incremental variance. If the one-year IV were 18%, total variance would instead be 0.0324, below 0.045.

A distinction for surfaces with a smile

At a fixed log-moneyness, an increasing w(k,T)w(k,T) is the appropriate calendar restriction in the deterministic proportional-carry setting developed below. Its maturity derivative should not generally be called the risk-neutral expected instantaneous variance of the underlying. A single smile point is a contract-level Black equivalent, while variance-swap expectations aggregate option prices across strikes.

ATM total variance is a convenient term-structure input for SSVI. The reference example uses a positive exponentially relaxing variance rate. Its short limit is 24% and its long volatility limit 18%, while total variance remains increasing. These are parameters of a synthetic surface, not estimated market forecasts.

Variance swaps and volatility indices

Under a positive continuous-price framework, a log-contract replication motivates an idealized variance-swap strike expressed using out-of-the-money option prices. With suitable integrability and no jump correction:

Kvar≈2TD(T)[∫0F(T)P(K,T)K2dK+∫F(T)∞C(K,T)K2dK].K_{\mathrm{var}}\approx \frac{2}{TD(T)} \left[\int_0^{F(T)}\frac{P(K,T)}{K^2}\,dK+ \int_{F(T)}^\infty\frac{C(K,T)}{K^2}\,dK\right].
(12)

The continuum replication, a discrete exchange index and an ATM implied volatility are distinct quantities. Real implementations specify strike selection, truncation, settlement and interpolation. Cboe's mathematics methodology provides an example of a defined discrete calculation. This guide does not reproduce that index or its operational rules.

The tails matter because the integral reaches beyond actively quoted strikes. Extrapolation and jumps can change variance-related quantities even when near-ATM fit is excellent. A surface intended only for ordinary vanilla interpolation may need stronger tail validation before being used for variance products.

08 / Market data

Option-chain data and contract conventions

A credible calibration begins with a contract table and synchronized observations. Each row should identify the underlying, expiry timestamp, strike, call or put, exercise style, settlement style, currency, multiplier, premium units and quote timestamp. Store raw bid and ask separately from derived midpoint, forward and IV.

Expiry is a timestamp

Calendar days, trading days and actual year fractions are different conventions. An option expiring in a morning auction and one expiring at a closing print can have different residual lives on the same calendar date. Near expiry, several hours can materially change a recovered IV because Black prices depend on total standard deviation σT\sigma\sqrt T.

Choose a time-zone-aware valuation timestamp and an explicit year-fraction convention. For the numerical examples, TT is an already specified year fraction and no calendar approximation is hidden in the engine. Real market-data ingestion should preserve the raw timestamps needed to reproduce that conversion.

Price observations and trading activity

A last trade may be stale while the current bid and ask are fresh. Volume records historical activity; open interest records outstanding contracts and does not guarantee a tight executable market at the valuation time. A midpoint is an estimate, not a promise that the full desired trade can execute there.

Underlying prices and option quotes should refer to the same time window. A fast spot move between timestamps can create false parity errors and apparent negative time values. If snapshots are asynchronous, either reconstruct a common-time estimate with an explicit method or retain a timing uncertainty flag.

Corporate actions and special contracts

Splits, special dividends and adjusted deliverables can change strike, multiplier or the underlying basket. A contract that delivers a cash component and a nonstandard number of shares does not fit a simple standard-contract formula without adjustment. Combining adjusted and ordinary series in one strike table may make a sound pricing model look inconsistent.

Settlement against a future, an index opening value or cash spot can require different forward inputs. Futures-style margining can alter the interpretation of discounting. Record the instrument's actual payoff and payment timing rather than assigning a convention solely from its ticker.

Reproducible derived fields

Derived IV should carry the price source, pricing model, forward, discount factor, maturity and solver status used to produce it. A useful status vocabulary distinguishes valid finite root, intrinsic limit, outside-bound quote, low-vega unresolved root and missing input. Replacing all of these states with zero loses information.

Store values in numeric decimal units and format percentages only in the display layer. A model expecting 0.24 but receiving 24 can produce an apparently flat price at the volatility upper limit. Unit validation is part of the calculation, not an optional presentation detail.

The synthetic chain in the worked studies omits exchange microstructure deliberately. It fixes every forward and discount input, making any residual identifiable as a solver or model-fitting issue. A real deployment must add the timestamp, contract and quality controls described here.

09 / Carry inputs

Forward estimation, dividends and put–call parity

Implied volatility is sensitive to the forward used for inversion. A carry error can distort a whole smile in a structured way because it changes intrinsic value and the location of forward ATM. Estimate forwards before interpreting call–put discrepancies as differences in volatility.

F(T)=K+C(K,T)−P(K,T)D(T).F(T)=K+\frac{C(K,T)-P(K,T)}{D(T)}.
(13)

This identity applies to matched European calls and puts with the same payoff dates and settlement convention. Multiple liquid strike pairs supply several estimates of one expiry forward. Their dispersion is a useful quality diagnostic; it does not justify averaging across incompatible contract types.

Intervals from executable sides

Midpoint parity gives a central estimate. Bid and ask provide an interval because buying the call and selling the put has a different cash flow from the reverse package:

K+Cbid−PaskD≤F(T)≤K+Cask−PbidD.K+\frac{C_{\mathrm{bid}}-P_{\mathrm{ask}}}{D} \le F(T)\le K+\frac{C_{\mathrm{ask}}-P_{\mathrm{bid}}}{D}.
(14)

Transaction costs, financing and shorting constraints complicate an executable arbitrage interpretation. The interval remains a useful measurement range under the specified frictionless parity framework. If several liquid pairs have nonoverlapping intervals, inspect synchronization and conventions before fitting a smooth curve through them.

Continuous and discrete distributions

A constant proportional yield gives F=S0e(r−q)TF=S_0e^{(r-q)T}. Known deterministic cash dividends can instead be represented by subtracting their present values from spot before financing the prepaid forward, under the appropriate trading assumptions. This is a carry calculation; it does not automatically justify treating a discrete-dividend equity as a continuous-yield lognormal process for all option valuations.

Uncertain dividends and stock-borrow costs may be embedded in option-implied forwards. A discrepancy from a simple cash-financing calculation can reflect these risks or market frictions. Label the forward as option implied, model based or directly observed rather than asserting that every difference is a data error.

Sensitivity of recovered IV to the forward

At fixed observed call price, implicit differentiation gives dσ/dF=−CF/Vegad\sigma/dF=-C_F/\operatorname{Vega}. Since CF=DΦ(d1)>0C_F=D\Phi(d_1)>0, raising the assumed forward lowers the recovered call IV. For a put, PF=−DΦ(−d1)P_F=-D\Phi(-d_1), and the sign reverses. A forward error can therefore produce systematic disagreement between call and put IV.

Near intrinsic bounds, the wrong forward may eliminate the finite root entirely. A solver that simply clips such quotes to a chosen volatility can hide the original carry problem. Propagate the invalid-input status to the calibration stage and retain the price row for investigation.

Across expiries, forward interpolation should be coherent with the carry model and relevant event dates. A smooth implied-volatility term structure cannot compensate for a discontinuity introduced by an incorrectly timed dividend. Validate the forward curve separately from the volatility surface.

10 / Observation quality

Quote filtering, bid–ask intervals and uncertainty

Cleaning is a documented estimation policy. Reject missing or nonfinite prices, crossed markets, incompatible contracts and premiums outside valid price bounds under the chosen inputs. Flag stale quotes and low-vega observations. Preserve the original rows and the reason for each decision so that a changed filtering policy can be audited.

Price intervals become volatility intervals

Because Black price is monotone in volatility, valid bid and ask premiums invert into an ordered interval. The midpoint premium's IV generally differs from the average of bid IV and ask IV because inversion is nonlinear. Use the actual convention intended by the calibration objective.

If one endpoint lies below intrinsic value, a complete finite IV interval cannot be reported without qualification. Clipping that endpoint to intrinsic may be a documented measurement rule, but it changes the data and should be identified. A zero bid in a far wing can indicate insufficient price resolution, rather than a precise zero volatility.

Weighting observations

A simple premium objective is weighted least squares. An observation's width can inform its weight, but a tiny displayed spread is not necessarily trustworthy if the quote is stale. Combine spread, timestamp and contract quality rather than using spread as the sole definition of reliability.

Linterval(p)=∑i[max(Cibid−Ci(p),0,Ci(p)−Ciask)]2si2.L_{\mathrm{interval}}(p)=\sum_i \frac{\left[\max(C_i^{\mathrm{bid}}-C_i(p),\,0,\,C_i(p)-C_i^{\mathrm{ask}})\right]^2}{s_i^2}.
(15)

Here Ci(p)C_i(p) is the fitted model premium and si>0s_i>0 a chosen scale. The loss is zero when the model lies inside the observed market interval. This can avoid chasing arbitrary midpoint noise, while a separate regularization term chooses among many interval-consistent surfaces.

Outliers and robust losses

A robust loss can reduce the influence of unusual residuals, but an outlier may be a genuine event-sensitive contract or a signal of an incorrect forward. Inspect systematic patterns. An entire expiry shifted in one direction suggests a common input issue more readily than seventeen independent anomalous quotes.

Minimum vega thresholds should depend on premium precision and the intended use. A far-wing quote may be too weak to identify IV precisely yet still constrain a tail premium or a digital payoff. Excluding it from a point-IV fit does not mean it contains no economic information.

Measurement uncertainty versus model uncertainty

Bid–ask width describes a market interval under the snapshot. Sampling noise and stale observations add measurement uncertainty. Functional-form choice, missing wings, future smile dynamics and uncertain carry add model uncertainty. A parameter covariance matrix from a local optimizer addresses only part of this picture.

Resample plausible quotes within their intervals, alter quality thresholds and refit from multiple initial points. Compare the resulting prices and derivatives. A small midpoint RMSE can coexist with unstable local variance because differentiation amplifies noise. The target application determines which outputs need the strongest uncertainty assessment.

11 / Static consistency

Strike arbitrage: bounds, verticals and butterflies

A surface is statically consistent when its European option prices respect the payoff relationships that can be assembled today. Positive volatility is insufficient. An independently chosen IV for every strike can produce a call curve that increases with strike or becomes locally concave.

Price bounds and vertical spreads

For a positive underlying with forward FF, a European call lies between discounted intrinsic value and discounted forward value. At one maturity, the call payoff decreases as strike rises. The payoff difference between calls with strikes K1<K2K_1<K_2 lies between zero and K2−K1K_2-K_1, giving:

0≤C(K1,T)−C(K2,T)≤D(T)(K2−K1).0\le C(K_1,T)-C(K_2,T)\le D(T)(K_2-K_1).
(16)

In a differentiable continuum, the associated slope restriction is −D(T)≤CK≤0-D(T)\le C_K\le0. The upper bound prevents an increasing call curve. The lower bound prevents a vertical spread from costing more than its discounted maximum payoff.

Butterfly convexity

A symmetric strike butterfly is long calls at K−hK-h and K+hK+h, and short two calls at KK. Its terminal payoff is nonnegative. Its price must therefore be nonnegative:

C(K−h,T)−2C(K,T)+C(K+h,T)≥0,CKK(K,T)≥0.C(K-h,T)-2C(K,T)+C(K+h,T)\ge0,\qquad C_{KK}(K,T)\ge0.
(17)

For irregular strike spacing, compare consecutive secant slopes. The slope between K1,K2K_1,K_2 must not exceed the slope between K2,K3K_2,K_3. Using a symmetric finite-difference formula on an irregular chain can produce misleading signs.

These restrictions apply to option premiums at common expiry and carry inputs. They do not require implied volatility to be monotone or convex. A steep but economically admissible skew can have quite different geometry from the convex call-price function it generates.

Discrete tests and continuous extensions

A price table can pass every available-strike test while an interpolating curve violates convexity between those strikes. Conversely, a tiny negative estimated second derivative can result from finite precision. State the tested domain, step size and tolerance, and distinguish a payoff violation in raw quotes from a derivative violation introduced by fitting.

Bid and ask change the practical test. A midpoint butterfly can be negative even when the package cannot be bought at a negative executable price. For a long butterfly, its execution cost uses wing asks and center bids. A frictionless surface fit may still seek convexity, but the data diagnosis should not equate every midpoint inconsistency with an immediately tradable arbitrage.

A proper extension also needs terminal behavior: calls approach zero as strike tends to infinity, and approach DFDF as strike approaches zero for a nonnegative underlying with the stated mean. Local convexity without correct boundaries can describe an incomplete or misnormalized distribution.

12 / Cross-expiry consistency

Calendar ordering under deterministic carry

Calendar comparisons require a precise framework. Assume deterministic discounting and proportional carry, and a positive underlying whose forward-normalized price is a true martingale under the pricing measure. At a common forward-moneyness ratio, normalized call values should not decrease with maturity.

Let XT=ST/F(T)X_T=S_T/F(T) and x=K/F(T)x=K/F(T). The normalized call is an expectation of a convex payoff, c(x,T)=𝔼[(XT−x)+]c(x,T)=\mathbb E[(X_T-x)^+]. The martingale property and conditional Jensen inequality imply that a later XTX_T has at least as much convex-payoff value at the same xx.

C(F(T2)ek,T2)D(T2)F(T2)≥C(F(T1)ek,T1)D(T1)F(T1),T2>T1.\frac{C(F(T_2)e^k,T_2)}{D(T_2)F(T_2)} \ge \frac{C(F(T_1)e^k,T_1)}{D(T_1)F(T_1)}, \qquad T_2>T_1.
(18)

The normalized Black formula is increasing in total variance at fixed kk. Consequently the calendar restriction becomes:

w(k,T2)≥w(k,T1),∂Tw(k,T)≥0at fixed k.w(k,T_2)\ge w(k,T_1),\qquad \partial_T w(k,T)\ge0\quad\text{at fixed }k.
(19)

Why annualized volatility is the wrong test

A one-year IV of 25% accumulates more variance than a six-month IV of 30%. Requiring σ(k,T2)≥σ(k,T1)\sigma(k,T_2)\ge\sigma(k,T_1) would reject this valid possibility. The factor TT in w=Tσ2w=T\sigma^2 is essential.

Absolute strike and nonzero carry

With zero carry and constant discounting, a fixed strike is also a fixed forward-moneyness ratio. With nonzero carry, these coordinates differ. Checking raw call premiums at a fixed strike without normalizing can conflate discounting, forward movement and convex-order consistency.

The maturity derivative at fixed absolute strike includes the changing k(T)=ln(K/F(T))k(T)=\ln(K/F(T)). Under constant r,qr,q, dk/dT=−(r−q)dk/dT=-(r-q). A derivative reported as “calendar theta” must specify which coordinate is held fixed. The laboratory's calendar checks use fixed kk, while its selected option uses an explicit absolute strike reconstructed from the chosen forward ratio.

Limits of the argument

Discrete cash dividends can disrupt the simple forward-normalized martingale relationship used here. Stochastic rates, different settlement dates and early exercise also require a richer analysis. Apply the normalized total-variance condition within its assumptions; do not use it as a universal test for every option market.

Checking calendar ordering at a finite strike grid is useful but cannot prove the condition between or beyond sampled points. A parameterization with analytical sufficient conditions can supply stronger assurance. A proof for each separate smile still leaves cross-expiry ordering unresolved unless the smiles are linked coherently.

A calibration routine should distinguish failure of a sufficient certification bound from an observed negative calendar increment. The former means the selected proof does not apply; the latter is direct evidence of inconsistency on the tested domain. Reporting both prevents an absence-of-proof message from being confused with an actual arbitrage diagnosis.

13 / Distribution recovery

Risk-neutral density and smile derivatives

Assume a European call price can be written C(K,T)=D(T)∫K∞(s−K)pT(s)dsC(K,T)=D(T)\int_K^\infty(s-K)p_T(s)\,ds, with a sufficiently regular terminal density. Differentiating in strike first removes the payoff magnitude and then recovers the density:

CK(K,T)=−D(T)Pr(ST>K),CKK(K,T)=D(T)pT(K).C_K(K,T)=-D(T)\Pr(S_T>K),\qquad C_{KK}(K,T)=D(T)p_T(K).
(20)

This connection between option prices and state-contingent claims is associated with Breeden and Litzenberger (1978). Atoms require a distributional interpretation rather than an ordinary smooth density. A finite set of strikes identifies neither every tail nor a unique continuous interpolation.

Differentiating through the smile

When ww varies with kk, differentiating a Black premium requires derivatives of ww. Holding implied volatility fixed while taking strike derivatives would recover a different distribution. Direct chain-rule differentiation gives a convenient sign diagnostic:

g(k)=(1−kwk2w)2−wk24(1w+14)+wkk2.g(k)=\left(1-\frac{k w_k}{2w}\right)^2 -\frac{w_k^2}{4}\left(\frac{1}{w}+\frac{1}{4}\right) +\frac{w_{kk}}{2}.
(21)

At K=FekK=Fe^k, define d2=−k/w−w/2d_2=-k/\sqrt w-\sqrt w/2. The strike density implied by the fitted smile is:

pT(K)=φ(d2)Kwg(k).p_T(K)=\frac{\varphi(d_2)}{K\sqrt w}\,g(k).
(22)

The prefactor is strictly positive for positive K,wK,w. A negative gg therefore identifies a negative density and a concave call-price region. The formula also makes the numerical problem visible: first and second smile derivatives enter a quantity that should remain nonnegative.

Normalization and the forward moment

For a complete nonnegative-terminal-price distribution, check that integrated mass is one and its first moment is the forward. Positive density on a short interval alone establishes neither property. Missing wings can leave substantial probability or forward value outside the observed range.

The numerical study integrates the reference density over a very broad positive-strike range using log-strike quadrature. It reports both mass and mean, with the finite integration range disclosed. This verifies the chosen example numerically; analytical tail conditions remain the stronger basis for an unrestricted surface.

What the recovered density means

This is a risk-neutral pricing distribution under the selected carry assumptions. A heavier left tail indicates expensive downside states in that measure. Translating it into a physical crash probability requires a model for state-dependent risk premia. Similarly, its variance is not generally the square of a single ATM implied volatility.

Differentiation magnifies quote noise. Use a consistent smooth price representation, compare derivative step sizes and quantify uncertainty in recovered tail probabilities. A density plot without its fitted-price residuals, extrapolation assumptions and numerical checks can look more precise than its inputs justify.

14 / Functional estimation

Interpolation, smoothing and surface regularity

The market supplies observations at discrete strikes and expiries. Interpolation supplies values between them; smoothing also allows fitted values to differ from observations. Choose the representation and regularity to match the intended output. Pricing a vanilla between quoted strikes needs less derivative stability than constructing a local-volatility diffusion.

Interpolating option prices

Piecewise-linear call prices can preserve monotonicity and convexity if their node slopes satisfy the strike conditions. The resulting second derivative is concentrated at knots, corresponding to a discrete terminal distribution. This can be adequate for a simple static pricing table, but it is unsuitable as a smooth local-volatility input without further modeling.

A convex smooth price interpolation can supply an ordinary density. Boundary behavior and calendar restrictions still need enforcement. Repairing each expiry's convexity independently may move its prices enough to break cross-expiry ordering.

Interpolating total variance

Total variance is convenient for maturity interpolation. At fixed kk, a linear interpolation between ordered total-variance slices preserves that calendar ordering between the two nodes. It does not automatically preserve butterfly freedom because the density diagnostic is nonlinear in w,wk,wkkw,w_k,w_{kk}.

Piecewise-linear w(k)w(k) has derivative jumps. A cubic spline can overshoot and create negative curvature in prices. A shape-preserving interpolator such as PCHIP preserves selected geometric properties of its input data, not the complete no-arbitrage structure of option prices.

Regularization

A penalized fitting problem balances observation errors with a roughness measure. For example, one may penalize squared second derivatives in a chosen coordinate:

L(p)=Lquotes(p)+λk∫wkk(k,T)2dk+λT∫wTT(k,T)2dT.L(p)=L_{\mathrm{quotes}}(p)+ \lambda_k\int w_{kk}(k,T)^2\,dk+ \lambda_T\int w_{TT}(k,T)^2\,dT.
(23)

The penalty is a modeling choice with units that depend on coordinates and integration domain. A small λ\lambda may chase noise; a large one may erase event structure. Smoothness alone is not an arbitrage guarantee. Add explicit consistency constraints or use a parameter family with suitable analytical restrictions.

Derivative quality and boundary policy

For local-volatility use, ensure that ww, its first time derivative and first two strike derivatives exist and are numerically stable on the valuation domain. Knots, expiry transitions and event dates require an explicit policy. Finite differences across a maturity knot can mix two different local regimes.

Never let an interpolator's default extrapolation silently choose the tails. State a separate wing and long-maturity rule. Compare values, slopes and, when required, curvatures at the transition. A surface can fit every observation while its uncontrolled extrapolation dominates a variance swap or a deep-out-of-the-money exotic.

Retain the fitted premium residuals alongside the smooth plot. Visual elegance is a presentation property; economic admissibility and data agreement are calculation properties that require their own evidence.

15 / Parametric smiles

The raw SVI total-variance parameterization

Stochastic Volatility Inspired, or SVI, is a parsimonious representation of a single-expiry total-variance smile. In its raw form, it combines a linear asymmetry term with a smoothed absolute-value shape:

w(k)=a+b[ρ(k−m)+(k−m)2+s2],b≥0,|ρ|<1,s>0.w(k)=a+b\left[\rho(k-m)+\sqrt{(k-m)^2+s^2}\right], \qquad b\ge0,\quad |\rho|<1,\quad s>0.
(24)

The parameter aa shifts the variance level, bb scales the wings, ρ\rho creates asymmetry, mm moves the shape horizontally and ss smooths its center. Their effects overlap; aa is not generally ATM variance, and mm is not generally the location of the minimum.

Minimum and positivity

Differentiate the expression to find its minimum at k=m−ρs/1−ρ2k=m-\rho s/\sqrt{1-\rho^2}. The corresponding minimum total variance is a+bs1−ρ2a+bs\sqrt{1-\rho^2}. Hence positivity requires that quantity to be nonnegative; the fitted value should be strictly positive where a finite smooth IV is used.

wk=b[ρ+k−m(k−m)2+s2],wkk=bs2((k−m)2+s2)3/2.w_k=b\left[\rho+\frac{k-m}{\sqrt{(k-m)^2+s^2}}\right],\qquad w_{kk}=\frac{bs^2}{\left((k-m)^2+s^2\right)^{3/2}}.
(25)

Although this wkkw_{kk} is positive, the call density can still become negative because gg contains additional terms. A convex total-variance function is not equivalent to a convex call-price function.

Wing slopes

For large positive kk, the asymptotic slope is b(1+ρ)b(1+\rho). For large negative kk, the coefficient of |k||k| is b(1−ρ)b(1-\rho). The parameters therefore control the two tail slopes jointly. Necessary tail restrictions help eliminate obviously inadmissible candidates but do not settle behavior in the center.

Fitting and identifiability

With only a narrow ATM strike range, several parameter combinations can produce nearly identical prices. The wings may then be determined mainly by bounds and initialization. Inspect the outputs actually needed—premiums, ATM level, skew and tail slopes—rather than interpreting every raw parameter as an independently measured economic quantity.

Use transforms or bounds for b,s,ρb,s,\rho, enforce positive variance, and validate the resulting gg and boundaries. A good single-expiry fit says nothing about calendar ordering versus the next expiry. SSVI, developed in the next chapter, provides a linked surface representation that can be subjected to stronger consistency conditions.

The numerical calibration study fits raw SVI to thirteen noisy synthetic quotes and withholds four other strikes. It reports fit error and out-of-fit interpolation error separately. Its price and derivative diagnostics are validation of that fitted example, not a claim that every raw SVI calibration is automatically admissible.

16 / Surface construction

SSVI and a coherent maturity parameterization

Surface SVI links smiles through ATM total variance θ(T)\theta(T), an asymmetry parameter ρ\rho and a positive shape function φ\phi. Its mathematical definition is:

w(k,T)=θ(T)2[1+ρφ(θ(T))k+(φ(θ(T))k+ρ)2+1−ρ2].w(k,T)=\frac{\theta(T)}{2} \left[1+\rho\phi(\theta(T))k+ \sqrt{(\phi(\theta(T))k+\rho)^2+1-\rho^2}\right].
(26)

At k=0k=0, the square root is one, so w(0,T)=θ(T)w(0,T)=\theta(T). Fixing ρ\rho links the shape across expiries. More general maturity-dependent extensions exist, but they need their own calendar conditions.

Gatheral and Jacquier's SSVI analysis supplies analytical conditions for static consistency. For constant ρ\rho, a useful sufficient calendar condition is increasing θ\theta and 0≤∂θ(θφ)≤φ0\le\partial_\theta(\theta\phi)\le\phi. Sufficient butterfly bounds are:

θφ(θ)(1+|ρ|)<4,θφ(θ)2(1+|ρ|)≤4.\theta\phi(\theta)(1+|\rho|)<4,\qquad \theta\phi(\theta)^2(1+|\rho|)\le4.
(27)

These bounds are sufficient; failing them alone does not prove a finite-strike butterfly violation. Correct wing behavior and calendar assumptions are part of the complete analysis.

The specific family used here

Choose φ(θ)=η/(1+θ)\phi(\theta)=\eta/(1+\theta), with η≥0\eta\ge0, and integrate a positive exponentially relaxing variance rate:

θ(T)=vl2T+(vs2−vl2)b(1−e−T/b),vs>0,vl>0,b>0.\theta(T)=v_l^2T+(v_s^2-v_l^2)b(1-e^{-T/b}), \qquad v_s>0,\quad v_l>0,\quad b>0.
(28)

The symbols vs,vlv_s,v_l are short and long volatility scales; bb is a decay time in years. Differentiation gives θ'(T)=vl2+(vs2−vl2)e−T/b>0\theta'(T)=v_l^2+(v_s^2-v_l^2)e^{-T/b}>0. Thus total variance is increasing whether the volatility term structure slopes up or down.

Also ∂θ(θφ)=η/(1+θ)2\partial_\theta(\theta\phi)=\eta/(1+\theta)^2, between zero and φ\phi. The calendar sufficient condition follows directly. The two butterfly expressions reduce to elementary functions whose maxima can be checked without a grid.

supθ>0θφ(θ)(1+|ρ|)=η(1+|ρ|),supθ>0θφ(θ)2(1+|ρ|)=η2(1+|ρ|)4.\sup_{\theta>0}\theta\phi(\theta)(1+|\rho|)=\eta(1+|\rho|),\qquad \sup_{\theta>0}\theta\phi(\theta)^2(1+|\rho|) =\frac{\eta^2(1+|\rho|)}{4}.
(29)

The first supremum is a long-maturity limit; the second occurs at θ=1\theta=1. Requiring the first expression strictly below four and the second at most four provides a global sufficient certificate for this family. It is deliberately conservative at a limiting equality.

What the parameters control

The ATM skew satisfies wk(0,T)=θρφw_k(0,T)=\theta\rho\phi, giving σk(0,T)=ρφθ/T/2\sigma_k(0,T)=\rho\phi\sqrt{\theta/T}/2. The reference parameters produce a negative skew. Raising η\eta steepens wings and increases curvature without changing ATM variance. Changing ρ\rho changes both asymmetry and the consistency bounds.

For a finite horizon HH, use 0<θ≤θ(H)0<\theta\le\theta(H) when evaluating maxima. A surface can pass sufficient bounds over the displayed horizon while failing the stronger all-maturity bounds. The laboratory distinguishes these outcomes and reports sampled gg separately. It never treats a favorable plot on a limited grid as a universal proof.

17 / Parameter estimation

Calibration objectives and statistical weighting

Calibration chooses parameters to represent observed prices or their derived coordinates. The objective determines which contracts dominate the fit. Minimizing premium errors, IV errors and total-variance errors are different problems even when they describe the same observation table.

LC(p)=∑iωi(Ci(p)−Ciobs)2,Lσ(p)=∑iνi(σi(p)−σiobs)2.L_C(p)=\sum_i\omega_i(C_i(p)-C_i^{\mathrm{obs}})^2,\qquad L_\sigma(p)=\sum_i\nu_i(\sigma_i(p)-\sigma_i^{\mathrm{obs}})^2.
(30)

For small residuals, Ci(p)−Ciobs≈Vegai(σi(p)−σiobs)C_i(p)-C_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\approx\operatorname{Vega}_i(\sigma_i(p)-\sigma_i^{\mathrm{obs}}). An unweighted premium loss emphasizes large-vega contracts. An unweighted IV loss gives a low-vega wing quote similar numerical influence to an informative ATM quote, despite its much wider price-derived IV uncertainty.

Total-variance fitting

Total-variance residuals are natural for SVI. Since dw/dσ=2Tσdw/d\sigma=2T\sigma, equal variance weights imply different IV weights at different maturities and levels. To compare fitting policies, translate residuals back into premiums and quote intervals rather than reporting only the optimizer's internal loss.

Lw(p)=∑iαi(wi(p)−wiobs)2.L_w(p)=\sum_i\alpha_i(w_i(p)-w_i^{\mathrm{obs}})^2.
(31)

A scale can be chosen from the estimated variance uncertainty 2TσΔC/Vega2T\sigma\,\Delta C/\operatorname{Vega}, with floors that avoid extreme weights. Such a scale is a first-order approximation. Wide spreads or near-intrinsic quotes may require fitting premium intervals directly.

Constraints and penalties

The calibration should impose the intended domain restrictions: positive variance, permitted parameter ranges, price bounds, calendar ordering and butterfly conditions. Penalties discourage violations but may leave small negative regions. Hard constraints or analytically admissible parameter transforms give different guarantees.

A model can be too restrictive to pass exactly through every midpoint while respecting consistency. If the observations themselves contain conflicts, an exact midpoint fit may be undesirable. Report whether fitted prices lie within spreads and which observations are responsible for the remaining error.

Interpolation and held-out contracts

Withholding some strikes tests interpolation within an expiry. Withholding an expiry tests maturity interpolation. Neither is a temporal forecast test: all contracts may belong to the same snapshot. A forward-looking validation of smile dynamics needs later snapshots and a specified prediction or hedging task.

The numerical example generates seventeen one-year IV observations by adding small deterministic perturbations to the reference surface. Four strikes are withheld, leaving thirteen for an equal-weight total-variance fit. This establishes a reproducible fitting problem and reveals residuals in actual IV units, without attributing random market significance to a synthetic error.

Calibration quality should include at least price or IV residuals, comparison with quote uncertainty, stability across starts and consistency diagnostics. A tiny numerical loss is only one piece of evidence. It cannot validate an unobserved wing or a dynamic hedging assumption.

18 / Numerical calibration

Optimization, identifiability and parameter stability

Surface fitting is often a nonlinear constrained problem with correlated parameters. A robust procedure makes initialization, bounds, scaling, stopping rules and failure states explicit. Save the objective value and diagnostics from every start, including unsuccessful candidates.

A practical sequence

  1. Build synchronized European quote rows and fix the forward, discount and maturity inputs.
  2. Compute premium bounds, valid IV intervals and coordinate values; retain quality flags.
  3. Choose a fitting representation and a loss matched to quote uncertainty and intended use.
  4. Initialize parameters from ATM level, skew and wing behavior, then run several admissible starts.
  5. Select a converged candidate using the stated loss, and perform independent price and arbitrage checks.
  6. Evaluate held-out contracts, perturb inputs and record output sensitivity.

This sequence prevents the optimizer from compensating silently for a forward error or a unit mistake. Carry estimation and data repair should be visible upstream operations.

Transforms and numerical scaling

Positive parameters may be represented by exponentials and ρ\rho by a bounded transform. Extremely large transformed values can overflow or produce flat gradients, so bounded optimization may be preferable in a teaching implementation. Express loss components in comparable numerical scales to prevent a large maturity or premium bucket from dominating unintentionally.

For raw SVI, the positivity condition depends jointly on a,b,ρ,sa,b,\rho,s; bounding aa positive is sufficient for positive variance when b≥0b\ge0, but can exclude valid representations with negative aa. The worked example uses a positive-aa box suitable for its synthetic data. It does not present those bounds as a complete general SVI calibration policy.

Local identifiability

Let JijJ_{ij} be the derivative of residual ii with respect to parameter jj. Small singular values of JJ indicate directions in parameter space that the observations identify weakly. A local covariance estimate based on JTJJ^\mathsf TJ requires statistical error assumptions and can be unreliable near constraints or multiple optima.

Compare prices and Greeks from different near-optimal fits. If parameters vary substantially while premiums remain stable, the problem may be adequate for vanilla pricing but weak for extrapolation. If density or local volatility also varies substantially, the intended derivative use needs more data or regularization.

Warm starts and monitoring

A previous snapshot supplies a useful warm start. It can also lock the algorithm into an old solution when the market changes, so periodically compare with fresh starts. Temporal regularization can improve stability, but it should not suppress real event-driven changes or conceal a data break.

Define explicit success criteria beyond the optimizer's flag: bounded loss, valid prices, acceptable residuals versus spreads, nonnegative tested density and calendar increments, and reproducible results. Convergence means a numerical termination condition was met; it does not mean the fitted surface is economically valid.

19 / Validation

Static-arbitrage validation and certification

Validation should operate at several levels. Check raw quote relationships, fitted prices at observed contracts, a dense interpolation domain, and analytical tails or sufficient conditions where available. Each level answers a different question.

A price-based audit

Reprice calls and puts using the fitted IVs and independent carry inputs. Confirm parity, bounds, vertical slopes and irregular-strike butterfly inequalities. Compare repriced premiums with bid–ask intervals. Testing only the IV table misses errors in coordinate conversion and discounting.

For cross-expiry tests, reconstruct common kk values, calculate normalized premiums, and check increasing total variance under the stated assumptions. A chain on fixed absolute strikes should be converted carefully rather than compared row by row by strike label.

An analytic derivative audit

For smooth slices, calculate wk,wkkw_k,w_{kk} and g(k)g(k). For smooth maturity behavior, calculate ∂Tw\partial_Tw at fixed kk. Compare analytic derivatives with finite differences at representative points. If the two disagree, investigate implementation and step size before interpreting the sign economically.

Finite differences have truncation error for large steps and cancellation error for extremely small steps. Test several moderate steps and look for a stable region. An apparent negative value of order machine precision needs a different interpretation from a broad negative-density interval.

What a grid can establish

A dense grid can find a violation. Passing the grid establishes that none was found at those points and tolerances. It cannot prove positivity over every real strike or all future maturities. Expand the domain, inspect potential extrema and evaluate tail slopes separately.

A valid analytical sufficient certificate is stronger. The laboratory reports global or finite-horizon SSVI bounds when they pass. If both certificates fail but sampled gg remains positive, the output says that the surface is not certified by those bounds. If sampled g<0g<0, the negative value is direct evidence of a butterfly inconsistency.

Global interpretation

Static absence of arbitrage supplies consistency of the current vanilla price collection within the model assumptions. It does not certify a particular future smile law, eliminate transaction costs, validate a stochastic-rate extension or prove an American-exercise surface is appropriate.

Store the validation domain, tolerances, implementation version, parameter set and input snapshot with each result. A label such as “arbitrage free” without its conditions and scope is less informative than a reproducible certificate accompanied by a numerical report.

The reference example has an analytical sufficient certificate and numerical checks of the density and moments. The intentionally extreme-shape example fails numerical density checks. These two examples help distinguish a certificate, a sampled test and an observed violation.

20 / Tail behavior

Wing asymptotics and extrapolation risk

Quoted strikes cover only a finite region. Any price for a deeper wing uses an extrapolation assumption. A curve-fitting model can make those assumptions explicit, but it cannot turn missing tail observations into measured information.

Total-variance growth

Lee's moment formula connects extreme-strike total-variance slopes with finite moments of the terminal distribution. For a positive underlying, the right and left limiting upper slopes lie in the interval from zero to two. Using p*=sup{p≥0:𝔼[ST1+p]<∞}p^*=\sup\{p\ge0:\mathbb E[S_T^{1+p}]<\infty\}, the right-wing relation is:

lim supk→∞w(k,T)k=ψ(p*),ψ(p)=2−4(p2+p−p).\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{w(k,T)}{k} =\psi(p^*),\qquad \psi(p)=2-4\left(\sqrt{p^2+p}-p\right).
(32)

The analogous left relation uses negative moments of STS_T. This is an asymptotic statement. It is not a pointwise finite-strike restriction w(k,T)≤2|k|w(k,T)\le2|k|, which would incorrectly force ATM variance to zero.

Why the coordinate matters

A volatility polynomial that grows quadratically in |k||k| eventually produces total variance growing faster than linearly. Its far tail may therefore become inadmissible even if the observed range looks reasonable. A model with controlled linear total-variance wings is easier to audit.

For raw SVI, the left and right slopes are b(1−ρ)b(1-\rho) and b(1+ρ)b(1+\rho). For the reference SSVI family, they are θφ(1−ρ)/2\theta\phi(1-\rho)/2 and θφ(1+ρ)/2\theta\phi(1+\rho)/2. Keeping them below two addresses a tail requirement; central butterfly and maturity conditions remain necessary parts of the audit.

Boundary and transition choices

Fit an interior region and attach wings with an explicit matching policy. Value continuity is the minimum requirement. Smooth first derivatives reduce artificial delta and digital discontinuities; second-derivative continuity can matter for local-volatility use. A smooth attachment may still violate gg, so inspect the transition as well as the distant asymptote.

Near zero maturity, the surface should approach an appropriate payoff limit. With continuous diffusion assumptions, θ(T)→0\theta(T)\to0. A scheduled jump can create a discontinuity in the maturity variance budget and needs a different treatment. Long-maturity extrapolation similarly requires stated ATM growth and smile behavior.

Valuation sensitivity

Deep-wing options, digitals, barriers and variance-related products can be sensitive to an extrapolation that barely affects ATM premiums. Revalue them under several admissible tail policies. The dispersion is a measure of modeling dependence, not a statistical confidence interval unless a probability model for those policies is supplied.

A helpful report separates observed-domain fit, interpolated-domain diagnostics and extrapolated-domain assumptions. The reference surface permits calculations on wide domains because its functional form is explicit. The worked calibration still treats far-wing behavior as a consequence of a chosen model, rather than evidence from withheld nonexistent quotes.

21 / Dynamic interpretation

Dupire local volatility and derivative stability

A local-volatility model specifies a deterministic diffusion coefficient depending on time and the current asset level. Under deterministic rates and proportional dividends, its risk-neutral dynamics are:

dSt=(r(t)−q(t))Stdt+σloc(St,t)StdWt.dS_t=(r(t)-q(t))S_t\,dt+\sigma_{\mathrm{loc}}(S_t,t)S_t\,dW_t.
(33)

The local coefficient is not the same object as contract-level implied volatility. A vanilla option samples many future states and times, whereas local volatility describes uncertainty at a particular state and instant.

The forward pricing equation

For a sufficiently smooth European call surface C(K,T)C(K,T), with all strike derivatives taken at fixed TT and the time derivative at fixed absolute KK, the Dupire expression is:

σloc2(K,T)=CT+q(T)C+(r(T)−q(T))KCK12K2CKK.\sigma_{\mathrm{loc}}^2(K,T)= \frac{C_T+q(T)C+(r(T)-q(T))K C_K} {\frac{1}{2}K^2C_{KK}}.
(34)

The formula follows from integrating the forward density equation against the call payoff. It requires the model assumptions, a valid surface and appropriate boundary behavior. Columbia's model-risk lecture material discusses the distinction between implied and local surfaces.

In normalized forward log-moneyness coordinates, the equivalent expression is particularly compact:

σloc2(Fek,T)=∂Tw(k,T)g(k,T).\sigma_{\mathrm{loc}}^2(Fe^k,T)=\frac{\partial_T w(k,T)}{g(k,T)}.
(35)

The numerator holds kk fixed. This is consistent with the fixed-KK premium formula only after including its carry terms. Using a fixed-KK total-variance derivative without the coordinate conversion creates a different result.

Why local volatility is difficult to estimate

The numerator requires a maturity derivative and the denominator a second strike derivative. Both magnify observation noise and interpolation choices. A very small gg can amplify a small numerator error into a large local variance. Negative calendar increments or negative density yield a nonphysical coefficient.

Do not automatically clip negative local variance to zero and describe the output as calibrated. Clipping changes the dynamic model and breaks exact reproduction of the source prices. Investigate the input surface and regularity; if a repair is necessary, reprice the vanilla grid under the repaired model.

What vanilla matching can and cannot identify

Within the regular local-diffusion framework, a continuum of European prices can determine a local coefficient. Market observations are finite and noisy, so constructing that continuum requires estimation and boundary assumptions. Even an ideal vanilla-matching local model is only one possible dynamic explanation.

A stochastic-volatility model can share the same terminal marginals while producing different forward smiles and path-dependent values. Matching today's calls does not determine barrier-crossing probabilities uniquely. Validate an exotic model against information relevant to its path dependence, and examine sensitivity to dynamics.

The reference plots use analytic derivatives rather than noisy finite differences. This isolates the mathematical transformation from data-estimation difficulties. The laboratory displays local volatility for a selected contract only when its variance and density diagnostics permit a positive value.

22 / Alternative dynamics

Stochastic volatility, jumps and SABR

A static parameterization describes current vanilla prices directly. A stochastic model describes state variables and a law of motion, then derives those prices. It can be calibrated to a surface, but its usefulness also depends on whether its future smile behavior and hedge responses suit the application.

A stochastic variance example

The Heston model adds a mean-reverting square-root variance process:

dSt=(r−q)Stdt+vtStdWtS,dvt=κ(v¯−vt)dt+ξvtdWtv,dWtSdWtv=ρdt.dS_t=(r-q)S_t\,dt+\sqrt{v_t}S_t\,dW_t^S,\qquad dv_t=\kappa(\bar v-v_t)\,dt+\xi\sqrt{v_t}\,dW_t^v,\qquad dW_t^S\,dW_t^v=\rho\,dt.
(36)

Initial variance, long-run variance, mean reversion, volatility of variance and correlation influence the level, term structure and skew. Negative correlation can produce a downward smile asymmetry. These dynamic parameters are not interchangeable with similarly named shape parameters in an SVI fit.

Heston (1993) develops an option-pricing solution using this stochastic-volatility setting. Numerical calibration must still address integration conventions, parameter constraints and potential weak identification. A small residual at one snapshot need not select a unique dynamic parameter set.

SABR as a forward-based model

SABR models a forward and its stochastic scale, commonly under a suitable forward measure:

dFt=αtFtβdWt1,dαt=ναtdWt2,dWt1dWt2=ρdt.dF_t=\alpha_t F_t^\beta\,dW_t^1,\qquad d\alpha_t=\nu\alpha_t\,dW_t^2,\qquad dW_t^1\,dW_t^2=\rho\,dt.
(37)

The elasticity parameter β\beta affects how the diffusion scales with the forward; ν\nu governs volatility of the scale. Hagan, Kumar, Lesniewski and Woodward (2002) develop an asymptotic smile approximation and discuss smile-related hedge behavior.

An asymptotic implied-volatility formula has an approximation domain. Applying it to extremely long maturities or far wings does not guarantee admissible option prices. Normal, lognormal and shifted conventions also require care when forwards may be near or below zero. The positive-forward Black surface in this guide is not a direct solution to every interest-rate option convention.

Jumps and event risk

A jump component can produce non-Gaussian tails and distinctive short-expiry behavior. Its risk-neutral jump parameters may be weakly identified from a limited chain. Pricing methods, tail conditions and hedges differ from a continuous diffusion. In particular, a jump variance budget is not generally enough to price nonlinear option payoffs exactly.

Choosing a model for a task

For liquid European vanilla interpolation, a constrained surface representation may be sufficient. For path-dependent pricing, a dynamic model is required. For hedge analysis, evaluate the predicted relationship between spot moves and smile changes. For scenario generation, a physical measure may be needed rather than the risk-neutral calibration measure.

The choice should be assessed with out-of-fit prices, stability, relevant exotic observations if available, and hedge behavior. Extra parameters can improve a fit while increasing estimation uncertainty. A model is useful when its outputs remain interpretable and robust for the intended calculation.

23 / Risk measurement

Surface sensitivities and smile-motion conventions

The familiar Black Greeks differentiate a premium while holding specified inputs fixed. Once IV is a fitted function of strike, maturity and market state, a risk calculation must specify how that function changes when spot or another input is bumped.

Sticky strike

Under a sticky-strike scenario, IV at a fixed absolute strike and expiry is held constant as spot changes. For that option, delta is the ordinary Black spot delta under the given carry convention. This is a scenario assumption; the observed market surface need not move this way.

Sticky log-moneyness

Under sticky log-moneyness, σ(k,T)\sigma(k,T) remains fixed as a function, but a fixed strike moves to a different kk when the forward changes. If FF is proportional to spot, dk/dS=−1/Sdk/dS=-1/S. The total derivative of a call then becomes:

dCdS=ΔBlack+VegadσdS=ΔBlack−VegaSσk.\frac{dC}{dS} =\Delta_{\mathrm{Black}}+ \operatorname{Vega}\frac{d\sigma}{dS} =\Delta_{\mathrm{Black}}- \frac{\operatorname{Vega}}{S}\sigma_k.
(38)

For a negative local skew, the correction is positive: raising spot moves a fixed strike leftward in kk, increasing its IV under this particular sticky-moneyness rule. A different observed smile motion may reverse or modify that response.

Sticky delta and dynamic model Greeks

Sticky delta holds a delta-quoted representation fixed and requires an implicit coordinate conversion when spot moves. It is not generally identical to sticky log-moneyness because delta itself depends on volatility. A stochastic model supplies another rule through its state variables and calibrated parameter policy.

When recalibrating after a bump, specify which observed quotes are held fixed and which parameters may change. Recalibrated delta measures a different operation from differentiating a model with fixed parameters. The risk report should identify that operation clearly.

Higher-order and bucket sensitivities

Gamma includes second-order smile-motion terms. Vanna captures mixed spot–volatility dependence, and volga captures curvature in volatility. Surface buckets measure exposure to a localized quote or parameter change rather than a parallel IV shift. Their values depend on interpolation and recalibration rules.

To compute bucket vega, bump one market quote by a stated amount, rebuild the admissible surface and revalue the portfolio. The effect may spread across neighboring strikes and maturities because of shared parameters and constraints. A raw parameter derivative is not automatically an executable hedge ratio to a market contract.

Risk decomposition

For a small move, decompose price change into spot, carry, time and surface contributions under a chosen expansion. Large moves require full repricing and can make local Greek approximations inaccurate. Compare several smile-motion scenarios when the instrument is materially exposed to skew or wings.

The plotted comparison is a synthetic one-year call with strike 100. Its two deltas differ because the surface-motion rules differ, while both start from the same type of price map. The example demonstrates model dependence rather than ranking one rule as universally superior.

24 / Framework extensions

Scheduled events, dividends and exercise style

A smooth European proportional-carry surface is an effective central framework. Real instruments can violate its simplifying assumptions in specific, identifiable ways. Handling those features explicitly is more reliable than allowing a flexible smile fit to absorb them without explanation.

Scheduled-event variance

An earnings release, policy announcement or other scheduled event can affect expiries on opposite sides of the event very differently. A simple variance-budget illustration adds a nonnegative event increment after its date:

θ(T)=v2T+J1T≥te,J≥0.\theta(T)=v^2T+J\,\mathbf{1}_{T\ge t_e}, \qquad J\ge0.
(39)

This formula is an illustrative ATM budget. For a genuine jump distribution, exact option values depend on more than its variance, including asymmetry and higher moments. Black implied total variance need not equal a sum of diffusion variance and jump variance for every strike.

A maturity discontinuity is not compatible with the smooth derivative assumptions used in the basic Dupire expression at the event itself. A dynamic event model may use a jump kernel or separate pre-event and post-event evolution. Interpolating smoothly through the date can smear its risk into the wrong intervals.

Discrete dividends

A known cash dividend produces an asset-price jump under a standard equity model. It affects the forward and may alter exercise incentives. Replacing it with a constant yield can be a useful approximation for some contracts, but the approximation should be tested near ex-dividend dates and for large dividends relative to spot.

Uncertain dividends introduce additional pricing risk and option-implied carry uncertainty. Report their assumptions alongside the volatility surface. Otherwise a changed dividend forecast can be misreported as an isolated volatility shock.

American options

An American premium includes the value of optimal exercise when it matters. Inverting it through European Black prices can create artificial IV differences across puts and calls or strikes. An American implied-volatility calculation must use an exercise-aware pricing model, with consistent dividends, rates and borrow assumptions.

One may estimate a European-equivalent premium by subtracting a model-based exercise premium, then fit a European surface. The conversion inherits that model's uncertainty. It should be labeled and validated, particularly for deep in-the-money puts and dividend-sensitive calls.

Settlement and market-specific conventions

Different settlement times can cause same-date expiries to span different events. FX delta conventions, futures margining and negative-rate option conventions require their own data translation. There is no single IV field that automatically harmonizes all these markets.

The laboratory intentionally remains within a European deterministic-carry setup. These extensions are explained so that its mathematically consistent example can be transferred carefully rather than copied into a contract environment where its inputs no longer describe the payoff.

25 / Research practice

Implementation pipeline, monitoring and model risk

A production surface should be a reproducible calculation with recorded inputs, rather than a plot assembled from opaque IV fields. Separate ingestion, contract normalization, carry estimation, quote validation, inversion, fitting, consistency checks and downstream risk calculations.

Artifacts to retain

Save the raw snapshot, contract metadata, rates or discount factors, forward construction, accepted and rejected rows, fitted parameters, solver settings and validation report. Retain the model version and deterministic seed for any randomized procedure. These records allow a surprising density or hedge output to be traced back to its cause.

The fitting report should state loss units, observation weights, regularization, bounds, initializations and convergence. The validation report should state its strike and maturity domain, grids, derivative steps and tolerances, plus any analytical certificate. The downstream report should state extrapolation and smile-motion conventions.

Monitoring a sequence of snapshots

Track ATM level, skew, wing slopes, fit residuals versus spreads, rejected-quote counts, forward dispersion and consistency diagnostics. Sudden changes can reflect market events or data problems. A large parameter move accompanied by tiny price changes can instead indicate weak identification.

Monitor density and local-volatility outputs only on domains supported by the data and chosen extension. Large local-volatility spikes at maturity knots can be an interpolation issue rather than economic information. Keep the premium fit visible when reviewing derivative outputs.

Stress tests

Perturb spot, rates, dividends, timestamps, spreads and selected quotes. Compare admissible interpolation and extrapolation policies. Use alternative model families for instruments whose valuations depend materially on future dynamics. Separate the effects of measurement changes from changes in model assumptions.

A shock may make a previously admissible parameter set inadmissible. Recompute constraints after every proposed bump or refit. Clamping only the displayed IV or hiding negative density makes the chart cleaner while leaving the underlying valuation inconsistent.

Interpretation of research results

A surface is descriptive of option prices at a valuation time. A trading claim requires transaction costs, execution, later observations and a prediction target. A synthetic calibration error is a numerical demonstration, not a measure of achievable trading profit.

Out-of-sample pricing, temporal forecasting and hedging backtests are different experiments. Withheld strikes assess interpolation. Later-date quotes assess time evolution only if the forecasting rule was fixed beforehand. A hedge study assesses realized portfolio behavior under actual rebalancing and costs.

Implementation checks

Unit checks, round-trip inversion, put–call parity, price bounds and independent derivative comparisons cover the mathematical core. Browser checks cover reproducible controls, hover coordinates, downloads, keyboard and touch interaction, responsive layout and offline rendering. Both are necessary for this page: a correct formula with a misleading inspector is still an unreliable learning tool.

The following laboratory and studies expose their conventions directly. The appendix provides reference calculations that can be compared with another implementation before the methods are applied to real quote files.
